THE GILDED ROAD
Vol. I: The Muddy Heart

From the private journals of Auditor Crassius Palleon
[pagebreak]
4th of Sun's Dusk, 4E 201
I have finally arrived in Whiterun, and I am already reconsidering my life choices. The poets call it the "Heart of Skyrim." I call it a muddy hill populated by people who think shouting is a form of debate. The wind here cuts through you like a tax collector, and the smell is atrocious. It is the stench of wet dog and uncured leather. It permeates everything. However, where there is stench, there is opportunity. I visited the market today. It is a chaotic affair, overflowing with the harvest. The Nords here grow wheat and tundra cotton in such absurd quantities that I saw a beggar sleeping on a sack of grain that would have cost five Septims in the Imperial City. I spoke to a local butcher--a massive man with more hair on his arms than on his head. He sold me a side of beef for pennies. Pennies! I suspect they have so many cows on these plains that they view meat as a burden rather than a commodity. I have purchased a cartload of cured hides for a song. If I can get these to a city that actually knows how to make shoes, I shall triple my investment. [pagebreak]
7th of Sun's Dusk
I dined at Dragonsreach this evening. The Jarl seems a reasonable man, though his court is dreadfully drab. The food was hearty, I will admit, but completely devoid of flavor. Nords seem to believe that "salt" is a luxury spice. I brought a small pouch of Cyrodiilic spices with me--pepper, nutmeg, elf-clove. You should have seen their eyes. The Jarl's steward practically wept when he tasted the seasoned venison. I sold him the remaining ounce of pepper for enough gold to buy a horse. Note to self: The Nords are desperate for flavor and refinement. They walk around in furs and iron, looking like bears. I wore my simple gold signet ring and a velvet doublet, and I caught the court wizard staring at it with envy. There is no jewelry here, only steel trinkets. Next time, I shall bring gemstones and silk. I could buy the whole city with a box of necklaces. [pagebreak]
9th of Sun's Dusk
My ears are ringing. The sound of hammering never stops. Between the Warmaiden's shop at the gate and the Skyforge on the hill, this city produces enough iron and steel to arm every bandit from here to High Rock. I made the mistake of trying to sell a shipment of Imperial swords I had acquired. The blacksmith, a woman named Adrianne, looked at them, laughed, and offered me scrap value. "We have plenty of iron, milk-drinker," she said. A lesson learned. Bringing weapons to Whiterun is like bringing ice to a glacier. I shall leave the iron to them.

[pagebreak] _________________________
MEMORANDUM FOR THE LEDGER
ACQUIRE: Leather, Wheat, Tundra Cotton, Beef. (They practically give it away).
OFFLOAD: Jewelry, Fine Clothes, Gold, Silver. (The Jarls will pay double).
AVOID: Iron, Steel, Basic Weapons. (Market is saturated).
_________________________ [pagebreak]
Tomorrow, I depart for The Reach. I am told the terrain is treacherous and the natives--the Forsworn--are hostile. But Markarth sits atop a literal mountain of silver. The Silver-Blood family thinks they own it all. We shall see about that.
- C. Palleon

LA RUTA DORADA
Vol. I: El corazón de cieno

De los diarios privados del auditor Crassius Palleon
[pagebreak]
4 de El ocaso, 4E 201
Finalmente he llegado a Carrera Blanca, y ya estoy reconsiderando mis decisiones de vida. Los poetas la llaman el

. Yo la llamo una colina embarrada poblada por gente que cree que gritar es una forma de debate. El viento aquí te atraviesa como un recaudador de impuestos, y el olor es atroz. Es el hedor de un perro mojado y cuero sin curtir. Lo impregna todo. Sin embargo, donde hay hedor, hay oportunidad. Hoy visité el mercado. Es un asunto caótico, rebosante de la cosecha. Los nórdicos aquí cultivan trigo y algodón de tundra en cantidades tan absurdas que vi a un mendigo durmiendo sobre un saco de grano que habría costado cinco septims en la Ciudad Imperial. Hablé con un carnicero local; un hombre enorme con más pelo en los brazos que en la cabeza. Me vendió una pieza de carne de buey por peniques. ¡Peniques! Sospecho que tienen tantas vacas en estas llanuras que ven la carne como una carga más que como una mercancía. He comprado un cargamento de pieles curtidas por una miseria. Si logro llevar esto a una ciudad donde realmente sepan fabricar zapatos, triplicaré mi inversión. [pagebreak]
7 de El ocaso
Cené en Cuenca Dragón esta noche. El jarl parece un hombre razonable, aunque su corte es terriblemente sosa. La comida era sustanciosa, debo admitirlo, pero completamente carente de sabor. Los nórdicos parecen creer que la

es una especia de lujo. Traje conmigo una pequeña bolsa de especias de Cyrodiil: pimienta, nuez moscada, clavo de elfo. Deberías haber visto sus ojos. El administrador del jarl prácticamente lloró cuando probó el venado sazonado. Le vendí la onza restante de pimienta por suficiente oro para comprar un caballo. Nota mental: los nórdicos están desesperados por sabor y refinamiento. Caminan envueltos en pieles e hierro, pareciendo osos. Yo llevaba mi sencillo sello de oro y un jubón de terciopelo, y sorprendí al mago de la corte mirándolo con envidia. Aquí no hay joyería, solo baratijas de acero. La próxima vez traeré gemas y seda. Podría comprar la ciudad entera con una caja de collares. [pagebreak]
9 de El ocaso
Me zumban los oídos. El sonido de los martillazos nunca cesa. Entre la tienda de la Doncella Guerrera junto a la puerta y la Forja del Cielo en la colina, esta ciudad produce suficiente hierro y acero para armar a cada bandido desde aquí hasta Roca Alta. Cometí el error de intentar vender un cargamento de espadas imperiales que había adquirido. La herrera, una mujer llamada Adrianne, las miró, se rió y me ofreció su valor como chatarra. "Tenemos hierro de sobra, bebedor de leche", dijo. Lección aprendida. Traer armas a Carrera Blanca es como traer hielo a un glaciar. Les dejaré el hierro a ellos.

[pagebreak] _________________________
MEMORÁNDUM PARA EL LIBRO DE CONTABILIDAD
ADQUIRIR: Cuero, trigo, algodón de tundra, carne de buey. (Prácticamente lo regalan).
VENDER: Joyas, ropa fina, oro, plata. (Los jarls pagarán el doble).
EVITAR: Hierro, acero, armas básicas. (El mercado está saturado).
_________________________ [pagebreak]
Mañana parto hacia La Cuenca. Me han dicho que el terreno es traicionero y los nativos —los Renegados— son hostiles. Pero Markarth se asienta sobre una montaña literal de plata. La familia Sangre Argéntea cree que lo posee todo. Ya lo veremos.
- C. Palleon

THE GILDED ROAD
Vol. II: The City of Stone

From the private journals of Auditor Crassius Palleon
[pagebreak]
12th of Sun's Dusk, 4E 201
If Whiterun was a muddy pigsty, The Reach is a vertical deathtrap.
The carriage ride here took five years off my life. We were ambushed twice by "Forsworn"--savages wearing antlers and very little else. My hired guards managed to fend them off, but I spent the entire journey huddled under a tarp, clutching my ledger.
Markarth itself is impressive, I suppose, if you enjoy living inside a tomb. It is an ancient Dwarven fortress, entirely gray, entirely stone, and entirely depressing. My room at the Silver-Blood Inn has a stone bed. Stone. My spine may never recover. [pagebreak]
14th of Sun's Dusk
I have been observing the local economy. It is completely broken, which is wonderful news for me.
The Silver-Blood family runs this city like a personal fiefdom. They own Cidhna Mine, the most productive silver prison in Tamriel. Because of this, silver and gold are treated like common gravel here. I watched a smith melt down a silver ingot just to fix a pot handle.
I purchased a dozen bars of refined silver for a price that would be considered theft in the Imperial City. They have so much of it, they don't know what it's worth to the outside world.
However, do not ask for a salad.
The terrain here is all crag and rock. Nothing grows. I saw a merchant selling a single withered leek for five septims. I sold the rest of my grain and dried beef from Whiterun within an hour of arriving. The locals are starving for anything that isn't goat meat or moss. [pagebreak]
15th of Sun's Dusk
There is another opportunity here: Dwemer Scrap.
The city is built on top of a ruin. The Jarl's court wizard, Calcelmo, is obsessed with the stuff, but the common markets are cluttered with bent cogs and strange metal struts. It's heavy, useless junk to them. But I know smiths in Solitude who would kill to study this metal.
I also noted a severe lack of timber. Since trees don't grow on cliffs, firewood is a luxury item. If I had brought a cart of lumber instead of my own luggage, I could have retired today. [pagebreak]
16th of Sun's Dusk
I am leaving. The stone bed is destroying my back, and the guards look at everyone as if they are criminals.
I have hired a new carriage. The cart is groaning under the weight of silver ingots and Dwarven metal. It will be a slow journey east, but a profitable one. [pagebreak] _________________________
MEMORANDUM FOR THE LEDGER
ACQUIRE: Silver, Gold, Dwemer Scrap. (The mines produce endless supply).
OFFLOAD: Food (Vegetables/Grain), Wood, Leather, Ale. (They cannot farm on rocks).
AVOID: selling Mining products, ores and ingots (Obvious reasons).
_________________________
Next, I head for The Rift. I am told the Thieves Guild runs the place, but frankly, after dealing with the Silver-Bloods, I prefer honest criminals. At least Riften has a lake, and more importantly, the Black-Briar Meadery. I need a drink.
- C. Palleon

LA RUTA DORADA
Vol. II: La ciudad de piedra

De los diarios privados del auditor Crassius Palleon
[pagebreak]
12 de El ocaso, 4E 201
Si Carrera Blanca era una pocilga de lodo, La Cuenca es una trampa mortal vertical.
El viaje en carruaje me quitó cinco años de vida. Fuimos emboscados dos veces por "Renegados" —salvajes que visten cornamentas y muy poco más. Mis guardias contratados lograron repelerlos, pero pasé todo el trayecto acurrucado bajo una lona, aferrado a mi libro de contabilidad.
Markarth en sí es impresionante, supongo, si disfrutas viviendo dentro de una tumba. Es una antigua fortaleza enana, enteramente gris, enteramente de piedra y enteramente deprimente. Mi habitación en la posada de Sangre Argéntea tiene una cama de piedra. De piedra. Es posible que mi columna nunca se recupere. [pagebreak]
14 de El ocaso
He estado observando la economía local. Está completamente rota, lo cual es una noticia maravillosa para mí.
La familia Sangre Argéntea dirige esta ciudad como un feudo personal. Son dueños de la mina de Cidhna, la prisión de plata más productiva de Tamriel. Debido a esto, la plata y el oro son tratados como grava común aquí. Vi a un herrero fundir un lingote de plata solo para arreglar el asa de una olla.
Compré una docena de barras de plata refinada por un precio que sería considerado un robo en la Ciudad Imperial. Tienen tanta que no saben lo que vale para el mundo exterior.
Sin embargo, no pidas una ensalada.
El terreno aquí es todo risco y roca. Nada crece. Vi a un comerciante vendiendo un solo puerro marchito por cinco septims. Vendí el resto de mi grano y carne seca de Carrera Blanca a la hora de haber llegado. Los lugareños están hambrientos de cualquier cosa que no sea carne de cabra o musgo. [pagebreak]
15 de El ocaso
Hay otra oportunidad aquí: chatarra dwemer.
La ciudad está construida sobre una ruina. El mago de la corte del jarl, Calcelmo, está obsesionado con esas cosas, pero los mercados comunes están abarrotados de engranajes doblados y extraños puntales de metal. Para ellos es basura pesada e inútil. Pero conozco herreros en Soledad que matarían por estudiar este metal.
También noté una grave falta de madera. Dado que los árboles no crecen en los acantilados, la leña es un artículo de lujo. Si hubiera traído un carro de madera en lugar de mi propio equipaje, podría haberme jubilado hoy mismo. [pagebreak]
16 de El ocaso
Me marcho. La cama de piedra está destruyendo mi espalda, y los guardias miran a todo el mundo como si fueran criminales.
He contratado un nuevo carruaje. El carro gime bajo el peso de los lingotes de plata y el metal enano. Será un viaje lento hacia el este, pero provechoso. [pagebreak] _________________________
MEMORÁNDUM PARA EL LIBRO DE CONTABILIDAD
ADQUIRIR: Plata, oro, chatarra dwemer. (Las minas producen un suministro infinito).
VENDER: Comida (verduras/grano), madera, cuero, cerveza ale. (No pueden cultivar sobre las rocas).
EVITAR: vender productos mineros, minerales y lingotes. (Razones obvias).
_________________________
A continuación, me dirijo a La Grieta. Me han dicho que el Gremio de Ladrones dirige el lugar, pero francamente, después de tratar con los Sangre Argéntea, prefiero criminales honestos. Al menos Riften tiene un lago y, lo más importante, la destilería Espina Negra. Necesito un trago.
- C. Palleon

THE GILDED ROAD
Vol. III: The Golden Rot

From the private journals of Auditor Crassius Palleon
[pagebreak]
20th of Sun's Dusk, 4E 201
Riften is a paradox. From a distance, it is beautiful--bathed in the golden light of the autumn forest. Up close, however, it is a sewer with a city built on top of it. I was stopped by a guard at the gate who demanded a "Visitor's Tax." I recognized the grift immediately. I didn't pay him because I was intimidated; I paid him because I appreciate a man who knows his market value. This city is run by two things: Mead and Crime. I secured a meeting with Maven Black-Briar. A terrifying woman. I like her immediately. Her meadery produces so much Black-Briar Mead that the locals drink it like water. I purchased twenty crates of the "Reserve" label. In Solitude, this will sell as a high-end vintage. Here? It is cheaper than milk. [pagebreak]
22nd of Sun's Dusk
The docks are a hive of activity, though half the workers look like they would stab you for a sweetroll. The lake provides an endless supply of Salmon and Slaughterfish. However, I noticed a critical failing in their supply chain: Preservation. They catch more than they can cure. I sold the last of my Salt Pile reserves to the fishery. They paid triple the standard rate. If you are coming to Riften, bring salt. Without it, their entire economy rots in the sun. [pagebreak]
24th of Sun's Dusk
I visited the local smith, Balimund. A talented man, but he is obsessed with "Fire Salts" and works almost exclusively in leather and light steel for the... "traveling" population. This created a fascinating opportunity. While the thieves wear leather, the City Guards and Maven's mercenaries require Heavy Armor to intimidate the rabble. Because the local industry is so focused on stealth gear, there is a severe shortage of plate mail for the enforcers. I sold a shipment of Orcish Plate and Iron Shields to the Jarl's steward for a fortune. In a city of criminals, the business of being a jailor is quite profitable, and they pay handsomely for the equipment to do it. [pagebreak]
25th of Sun's Dusk
I am leaving before I lose my purse. The air here is thick with secrets, and I prefer my business conducted in the open (or at least, behind a sturdy desk). I have my mead, I have my leather, and I still have my head. A successful trip. [pagebreak] _________________________
MEMORANDUM FOR THE LEDGER
ACQUIRE: Black-Briar Mead, Fish, Light Armor. (The abundance of thieves drives light gear prices down).
OFFLOAD: Salt (For fish curing), Heavy Armor (For the guards).
AVOID: Selling Alchemy ingredients (The forest overflows the Market).
_________________________ [pagebreak] Next, I travel to the capital, Solitude. Finally, civilization. I look forward to selling this mead to the Emperor's cousins and sleeping in a bed that doesn't smell like wet rat.
- C. Palleon

LA RUTA DORADA
Vol. III: La podredumbre dorada

De los diarios privados del auditor Crassius Palleon
[pagebreak]
20 de El ocaso, 4E 201
Riften es una paradoja. De lejos es hermosa, bañada en la luz dorada del bosque de otoño. De cerca, sin embargo, es una alcantarilla con una ciudad construida encima. Un guardia me detuvo en la puerta exigiendo un "impuesto de visitante". Reconocí la estafa de inmediato. No le pagué porque me sintiera intimidado; le pagué porque aprecio a un hombre que conoce su valor de mercado. Esta ciudad funciona gracias a dos cosas: aguamiel y crimen. Conseguí una reunión con Maven Espino Negro. Una mujer aterradora. Me cayó bien de inmediato. Su destilería produce tanta Aguamiel de Espino Negro que los lugareños la beben como agua. Compré veinte cajas de la etiqueta "Reserva". En Soledad, esto se venderá como una cosecha de alta gama. ¿Aquí? Es más barata que la leche. [pagebreak]
22 de El ocaso
Los muelles son un hervidero de actividad, aunque la mitad de los trabajadores parecen capaces de apuñalarte por un bollo dulce. El lago provee un suministro infinito de salmón y pez asesino. Sin embargo, noté un fallo crítico en su cadena de suministro: la conservación. Pescan más de lo que pueden curar. Vendí lo último de mis reservas de montones de sal a la pesquería. Pagaron el triple de la tarifa estándar. Si vienes a Riften, trae sal. Sin ella, toda su economía se pudre al sol. [pagebreak]
24 de El ocaso
Visité al herrero local, Balimund. Un hombre talentoso, pero está obsesionado con las "sales de fuego" y trabaja casi exclusivamente en cuero y acero ligero para la población... "viajera". Esto creó una oportunidad fascinante. Mientras los ladrones visten cuero, los guardias de la ciudad y los mercenarios de Maven requieren armadura pesada para intimidar a la chusma. Como la industria local está tan centrada en el equipo de sigilo, hay una grave escasez de cota de placas para los ejecutores. Vendí un cargamento de placas orcas y escudos de hierro al administrador del jarl por una fortuna. En una ciudad de criminales, el negocio de ser carcelero es bastante rentable, y pagan generosamente por el equipo para hacerlo. [pagebreak]
25 de El ocaso
Me marcho antes de perder mi bolsa. El aire aquí es denso con secretos, y prefiero que mis negocios se realicen al descubierto (o al menos, detrás de un escritorio robusto). Tengo mi aguamiel, tengo mi cuero, y aún tengo mi cabeza. Un viaje exitoso. [pagebreak] _________________________
MEMORÁNDUM PARA EL LIBRO DE CONTABILIDAD
ADQUIRIR: Aguamiel de Espino Negro, pescado, armadura ligera. (La abundancia de ladrones baja los precios del equipo ligero).
VENDER: Sal (para curar pescado), armadura pesada (para los guardias).
EVITAR: Vender ingredientes de alquimia (El bosque inunda el mercado).
_________________________ [pagebreak] A continuación, viajo a la capital, Soledad. Finalmente, civilización. Espero vender esta aguamiel a los primos del Emperador y dormir en una cama que no huela a rata mojada.
- C. Palleon

THE GILDED ROAD
Vol. IV: The Imperial Seat

From the private journals of Auditor Crassius Palleon
[pagebreak]
2nd of Evening Star, 4E 201
Civilization, at last. Solitude is the only place in Skyrim where a man can find a bath that doesn't involve a bucket of ice water. The architecture is familiar, the stone is paved, and the guards actually polish their armor. I headed straight for the Blue Palace with the Black-Briar Mead I acquired in Riften. The irony is delicious. The courtiers here turn their noses up at the "criminal filth" of the Rift, yet they guzzled the mead the moment I told them it was a "Southern Reserve Vintage." I sold the entire shipment for a 400% markup. Whatever you do, do not tell them it costs ten septims a bottle at the source. [pagebreak]
5th of Evening Star
While the city is refined, it produces almost nothing of practical value. It is a city of consumers. I visited Radiant Raiment. The Altmer sisters who run it are insufferable shrews, but their work is exquisite. You cannot find Fine Clothes or Jewelry of this quality anywhere else in the province. I purchased five crates of velvet doublets and gold-threaded tunics. In the rougher holds like Windhelm or Dawnstar, the Jarls are desperate to look like nobility. They will pay a fortune for these "Imperial fashions." [pagebreak]
7th of Evening Star
I stopped by the East Empire Company warehouse today. Vittoria Vici is running the place. She is competent, but the war has strangled their supply lines. They are desperate for Raw Materials. The Legion needs weapons and armor, but Solitude has no mines and no farms. They import everything. The local smith, Beirand, practically begged me for Iron Ingots and Leather. If you have ore from Markarth or hides from the Whiterun plains, sell them here. The Legion pays better than any village smith, and their coin is always good. [pagebreak] _________________________
MEMORANDUM FOR THE LEDGER
ACQUIRE: Fine Clothes, Jewelry (The only luxury market in Skyrim).
OFFLOAD: Mead (Rebrand it), Ores, Ingots, Leather. (The Legion is hungry for war supplies).
AVOID: Buying basic gear. (Everything here is taxed to Oblivion).
_________________________
8th of Evening Star
I am preparing to leave. The Bards College is practicing some dreadful drum solo next door, and I can no longer think. My cart is lighter now, filled only with expensive silks and spices. I head East, into the snow, toward Windhelm. I suspect Ulfric Stormcloak will hate my Imperial face, but he will love the Imperial steel I am smuggling in under these clothes. War is, after all, the most profitable business of all. - C. Palleon

LA RUTA DORADA
Vol. IV: La sede imperial

De los diarios privados del auditor Crassius Palleon
[pagebreak]
2 de La estrella vespertina, 4E 201
Civilización, por fin. Soledad es el único lugar en Skyrim donde un hombre puede encontrar un baño que no implique un cubo de agua helada. La arquitectura es familiar, la piedra está pavimentada y los guardias realmente pulen su armadura. Me dirigí directamente al Palacio Azul con la Aguamiel de Espino Negro que adquirí en Riften. La ironía es deliciosa. Los cortesanos aquí miran por encima del hombro a la "suciedad criminal" de La Grieta, sin embargo, engulleron la aguamiel en el momento en que les dije que era una "Cosecha de Reserva del Sur". Vendí el cargamento entero con un margen del 400%. Hagas lo que hagas, no les digas que cuesta diez septims la botella en origen. [pagebreak]
5 de La estrella vespertina
Aunque la ciudad es refinada, no produce casi nada de valor práctico. Es una ciudad de consumidores. Visité Ropajes Radiantes. Las hermanas Altmer que lo dirigen son unas arpías insufribles, pero su trabajo es exquisito. No puedes encontrar ropas refinadas ni joyería de esta calidad en ningún otro lugar de la provincia. Compré cinco cajas de jubones de terciopelo y túnicas con hilo de oro. En las comarcas más rudas como Ventalia o Lucero del Alba, los jarls están desesperados por parecer nobleza. Pagarán una fortuna por estas "modas imperiales". [pagebreak]
7 de La estrella vespertina
Hoy pasé por el almacén de la Compañía del Imperio Oriental. Vittoria Vici dirige el lugar. Es competente, pero la guerra ha estrangulado sus líneas de suministro. Están desesperados por materias primas. La Legión necesita armas y armaduras, pero Soledad no tiene minas ni granjas. Importan todo. El herrero local, Beirand, prácticamente me rogó por lingotes de hierro y cuero. Si tienes mineral de Markarth o pieles de las llanuras de Carrera Blanca, véndelos aquí. La Legión paga mejor que cualquier herrero de pueblo, y su moneda siempre es buena. [pagebreak] _________________________
MEMORÁNDUM PARA EL LIBRO DE CONTABILIDAD
ADQUIRIR: Ropas refinadas, joyería (El único mercado de lujo en Skyrim).
VENDER: Aguamiel (cámbiale la marca), minerales, lingotes, cuero. (La Legión está hambrienta de suministros de guerra).
EVITAR: Comprar equipo básico. (Aquí todo tiene impuestos hasta en Oblivion).
_________________________
8 de La estrella vespertina
Me estoy preparando para partir. El Colegio de Bardos está practicando un espantoso solo de tambor al lado, y ya no puedo pensar. Mi carro es más ligero ahora, lleno solo con sedas caras y especias. Me dirijo al este, hacia la nieve, hacia Ventalia. Sospecho que Ulfric Capa de la Tormenta odiará mi cara imperial, pero amará el acero imperial que estoy introduciendo de contrabando bajo estas ropas. La guerra es, después de todo, el negocio más rentable de todos.
- C. Palleon

THE GILDED ROAD
Vol. V: The City of Granite and Ice

From the private journals of Auditor Crassius Palleon
[pagebreak]
10th of Evening Star, 4E 201
Windhelm. The city of kings, or so they claim. To me, it looks like a tomb carved from ice and granite. The guards eyed my cart with suspicion until I showed them the Fine Clothes I brought from Solitude. War makes men desperate to prove they are civilized. I sold the velvet doublets to a Stormcloak commander who wanted to look like a Jarl. He paid in silver, unaware that the fabric cost me a fraction of that in the capital. Here, Fabrics and luxury goods are in high demand because everyone is focused on steel and blood. They have no weavers, only smiths. [pagebreak]
11th of Evening Star
The market here is a paradox. The city is starving for Crops and Wood,the ground is too frozen to farm, and the war consumes all the timber. I saw a turnip sell for the price of a dagger. But if you need to kill a man, this is the cheapest place in Tamriel to buy the tool to do it. [cite_start]The "War Machine" is churning[cite: 1]. Every forge is hot. [cite_start]Weapons and Heavy Armor are being piled high in the streets[cite: 1]. [cite_start]Because of the nearby Gloombound Mine, Ebony is traded here as casually as iron is in Whiterun[cite: 1]. I purchased a set of Ebony gauntlets for a price that would make a Cyrodiilic merchant faint. [pagebreak] _________________________
MEMORANDUM FOR THE LEDGER
ACQUIRE: Ebony, Weapons, Heavy Armor, Horker Meat. (The war effort and local mines make these dirt cheap).
OFFLOAD: Crops, Wood, Fabrics (Fine Clothes). (They cannot farm, and they have no luxury industry).
AVOID: Buying Food. (Scarcity drives the prices to the sky).
_________________________
12th of Evening Star
[cite_start]I am loading the cart with Horker Meat and as many Greatswords as the axles can hold[cite: 1]. [cite_start]It is a heavy haul, dubbed "The War Profiteer" by the caravan drivers[cite: 1]. Vol. VI: The Graveyard of the North

From the private journals of Auditor Crassius Palleon

18th of Evening Star, 4E 201
The air in Falkreath hangs heavy, wet, and smelling of damp earth. They call this the "Hold of the Dead," and one does not need to see the massive cemetery to understand why. The forest here is ancient, a sprawling canopy of pine that chokes out the sun and traps the mist against the ground. It is oppressive, gloomy, and utterly magnificent for business if you know what to look for. I arrived soaking wet, my boots caked in mud. The Jarl, a young man named Siddgeir, seems more interested in imported wine than governing. A lazy ruler is a merchant's blessing; he cares little for tariffs as long as his own cup is full. I gifted him a bottle of the Solitude Spiced Wine I had saved, and he practically gave me the key to the market. [pagebreak]
20th of Evening Star
If Skyrim has a spine, it is built from Falkreath timber. The sawmills here run day and night. The river powers the blades, slicing through massive trunks of pine that would cost a fortune in the treeless plains of Whiterun. Firewood and Lumber are not just abundant here; they are practically debris. I watched workers burn scrap wood that a freezing family in Winterhold would kill for. I purchased an entire wagon-load of seasoned timber for a handful of septims. In the tundra, where the only fuel is dried grass and cow dung, this wood will sell for ten times the purchase price. It is the "Timber Run," simple and reliable. [pagebreak]
21st of Evening Star
But it is not just wood. The forests are teeming with game. Every second man I meet is a hunter, smelling of blood and tanning oil. Leather and Hides are the true currency of the common folk here. I inspected a stack of bear pelts at the local trader, Gray Pine Goods. The quality was exceptional--thick, winter coats, properly cured. Because the supply is so high, the prices are laughable. I bought enough leather to outfit a Centurion's guard. However, do not expect to find good steel here. The local smith is a simple man who spends more time complaining about his brother than hammering iron. Heavy Armor and Quality Weapons are scarce. The guards look like they are wearing heirlooms from the Great War. [pagebreak] _________________________
MEMORANDUM FOR THE LEDGER
ACQUIRE: Firewood, Leather, Hides. (The forests provide an endless supply of fuel and furs).
OFFLOAD: Heavy Armor, Weapons, Metals, Luxury Items. (They lack good smiths; the nobility craves imports).
AVOID: Selling Wood or Basic Bows.
_________________________ [pagebreak]
22nd of Evening Star
I am preparing to depart before the gloom seeps into my own bones. The constant talk of graves and ancestors is tiring. I will head north toward the plains and into the bog. I heard Morthal commoners would pay double for amulets and soul gems, I think they believe them to be some kind of protection. My cart is creaking under the weight of timber and furs. It is a slow journey, but a profitable one. One final note: There doesn't seem to be college or academic presence. Books and magic are imported luxuries.
- C. Palleon

25th of Evening Star, 4E 201
If Falkreath is a graveyard, Morthal is the open sore of Skyrim. The air here tastes of stagnant water and decay. My boots have not been dry for three days. The town--if one can call a collection of sinking shacks a town--sits deep in the Hjalmarch marshes. It is isolated, superstitious, and utterly devoid of comfort. Naturally, the locals are desperate for anything that reminds them of the civilized world. I arrived with a shipment of Glazed Pottery and Silverware from Markarth. It seems frivolous, but people living in squalor will pay ridiculous sums for a clean plate to eat off of. I sold a silver candlestick to the innkeeper, Jonna, for enough gold to buy the inn itself. [pagebreak]
26th of Evening Star
There is no industry here. No mines, no farms, just the lumber mill and the swamp. But the swamp holds its own kind of gold, if you have the stomach to harvest it. I visited the local apothecary, a hut run by a woman named Lami. She deals in the things that grow in the dark: Deathbell, Swamp Fungal Pods, and Giant Lichen. In Solitude or the Imperial City, alchemists pay a premium for these reagents to brew poisons and cures. Here? They grow like weeds on the roadside. I filled three crates with enough toxic flora to kill half the Emperor's council. The cost was negligible. To the locals, I'm doing them a favor by weeding their gardens. [pagebreak]
27th of Evening Star
The Jarl, Idgrod Ravencrone, is... unsettled. She speaks in riddles and stares at things that aren't there. But her steward is practical enough. The guard force here is pitiful. They fight frostbite spiders and chaurus with rusted iron axes. I opened the "War Profiteer" reserve I held back from Windhelm--a small stock of Steel Weapons and Shields. The transaction was immediate. They didn't even haggle. In Hjalmarch, a sharp blade isn't a luxury; it's the only reason you wake up in the morning. I suspect Falion, the resident wizard, might have coin for Soul Gems, but he gave me a look that curdled the milk in my stomach, so I steered clear. [pagebreak] _________________________
MEMORANDUM FOR THE LEDGER
ACQUIRE: Alchemical Ingredients (Deathbell, Swamp Fungal Pods, Chaurus Eggs). (The swamp has rare toxins).
OFFLOAD: Quality Weapons, Magical Amulets or Items.
AVOID: Buying Luxury Clothes. (The mud ruins everything instantly).
_________________________ [pagebreak]

I am leaving this damp hellhole. The fog is getting thicker, and I swear I hear drums in the distance. I head North, into the biting wind, toward Dawnstar and the ruins of Winterhold. The miners in the Pale dig for Quicksilver, and the mages in Winterhold sit on mountains of soul gems, yet none of them have enough food to fill their bellies. I will trade these poisons for ore and magic, provided I don't freeze to death on the road. For those following my path: Watch your step in the marsh. The mud is deep, and not everything buried in it is dead. - C. Palleon

2nd of Morning Star, 4E 202
The new year finds me in the coldest circle of Oblivion. I have arrived in the Pale, a land of white blinding snow and black rock. Dawnstar is a hard town. The people here are worn down by the wind and plagued by sleeplessness--they speak of nightmares that haunt the entire population. Bad for morale, but excellent for business. I unloaded the last of the Spiced Wine and Silverware here. Men terrified of sleeping will pay anything for a strong drink or a comfort for their families. But the true wealth here is underground. Dawnstar sits atop the Iron-Breaker and Quicksilver mines. Quicksilver is rare, used for elven alloys, and in the capital, it costs a fortune. Here, I bought three crates of refined ingots for the price of common iron. [pagebreak]
4th of Morning Star
Before leaving Dawnstar, I visited the port. The ships that brave the Sea of Ghosts dock here to offload Salt. The "Salt Trade" is recession-proof. It preserves food and cures leather. I filled the gaps in my cart with heavy sacks of sea salt. It is dead weight now, but in the interior holds, it is worth its weight in silver. I am now loading up on Firewood and Salted Meat. The locals think I am mad to carry so much lumber, but they do not know where I am going. The road to Winterhold is open, and hunger waits at the end of it. [pagebreak]
6th of Morning Star
Winterhold. Or what is left of it. The city fell into the sea years ago, leaving only a few shivering hovels and the College looming above like a tombstone. This is the "Relief Convoy." The mages hoard knowledge but starve for supplies. I sold a single bundle of birch firewood for enough coin to buy a horse. Food and Warmth are the only currencies that matter here. The College wizards, detached from reality, happily traded valuable Soul Gems and Spell Tomes for sacks of flour and dried beef. I met a wizard named Phinis who traded me a filled Grand Soul Gem for a week's worth of rations. He thinks he got the better deal. I know I did. [pagebreak] _________________________
MEMORANDUM FOR THE LEDGER
ACQUIRE (Dawnstar): Quicksilver, Iron, Salt. (Mines and port trade make these abundant).
ACQUIRE (Winterhold): Soul Gems, Spell Tomes.
OFFLOAD: Firewood, Food, Alcohol. ( survival goods fetch 200%+ markup).
_________________________ [pagebreak]
8th of Morning Star
I am leaving this frozen wasteland before I lose my toes. My cart is heavy with Quicksilver, Salt, and magical artifacts. I will turn South, toward the "Golden Road" of Whiterun or perhaps East to the warmth of the Rift. The circle is complete. I have walked the Gilded Road from the opulent palaces of Solitude to the starving cliffs of Winterhold. Remember: Gold is not found in mines, traveler. It is found on the road.
- C. Palleon

[pagebreak]


The Whispering Claw

By Ra'zinda

THE CAT'S EYE FOR COIN
The Imperial writes many words about where to sell. He tells you to take wheat to the snow, and iron to the swamp. This is good advice for a beginner.
But Ra'zinda knows that who you sell to is just as important as where you go.
A wise merchant does not sell a diamond to a beggar. The beggar has no coin. A wise merchant finds the one with the specific hunger. Each profession in Skyrim has a hunger. Feed it, and your purse will grow heavy. THE SOOT-WALKERS (Blacksmiths)
The Nords who pound metal are strong, but they are also lazy. They hate leaving their fires.
If you bring them Ores and Ingots, they will pay you extra. Why? Because it means they do not have to swing a pickaxe in the cold. They can stay warm by the forge.
Ra'zinda's Rule: Never sell raw metal to a general merchant. Save it for the smith. He pays for the convenience. THE MIXERS (Alchemists)
The smooth-skins are squeamish. They do not like touching Spider Eggs, Troll Fat, or Giant Toes.
The Alchemists are different. They crave these disgusting things. Because they need them for their potions, and because they are too weak to hunt trolls themselves, they will pay a premium for Ingredients and Animal Parts.
What is trash to a hunter is gold to an Alchemist. THE STAR-GAZERS (Wizards)
Mages are the best customers. They are often lost in their books and have no concept of the value of gold.
If you find Soul Gems, Spell Tomes, or Scrolls, take them only to a Court Wizard or the College. They are desperate for magic. They will empty their pockets for a filled soul gem without bargaining. It is almost too easy to take their coin. THE BELLY-FILLERS (Innkeepers)
Skyrim is cold. Everyone is hungry. But the Innkeepers are always running out of fresh supplies.
If you have Raw Food, meat, vegetables, salt, sell it to the Innkeeper, not the market stalls. They need it now to feed their guests. A hungry guest leaves; a fed guest buys ale. The Innkeeper knows this, and pays you for the help. THE FAMILY (The Caravans)
And finally, there are Ra'zinda's kin. The Caravans.
We are not welcome in the cities. We cannot set up shops. But we have... connections.
If you find things that are "troublesome" to sell, Jewelry, Luxury Goods, or items the Jarls call "Illicit", bring them to us.
We do not ask where you got them. We only weigh the gold. We pay the best prices for the things others are too afraid to touch.
Walk on warm sands, merchant. [pagebreak]
AFTERWORD

To the traveler holding this book:

Thank you for walking The Gilded Road.

It was my goal to bring new life to the markets of Skyrim, making every septum earned feel like a victory. I hope these changes have made your journey richer and your burdens a little lighter.

May your pockets be heavy and your path be clear.

— Vuszu

LA RUTA DORADA
Vol. IX: La garra susurrante

Por Ra'zinda
[pagebreak]
EL OJO DE GATO PARA LA MONEDA
El imperial escribe muchas palabras sobre dónde vender. Te dice que lleves trigo a la nieve y hierro al pantano. Este es un buen consejo para un principiante.
Pero Ra'zinda sabe que a quién le vendes es tan importante como a dónde vas.
Un mercader sabio no le vende un diamante a un mendigo. El mendigo no tiene monedas. Un mercader sabio encuentra a aquel con el hambre específica. Cada profesión en Skyrim tiene un hambre. Aliméntala, y tu bolsa crecerá pesada. LOS CAMINANTES DEL HOLLÍN (Herreros)
Los nórdicos que golpean el metal son fuertes, pero también son perezosos. Odian dejar sus fuegos.
Si les traes minerales y lingotes, te pagarán extra. ¿Por qué? Porque significa que no tienen que blandir un pico en el frío. Pueden mantenerse calientes junto a la forja.
La regla de Ra'zinda: Nunca vendas metal crudo a un comerciante general. Guárdalo para el herrero. Él paga por la comodidad. LOS MEZCLADORES (Alquimistas)
Los pieles suaves son aprensivos. No les gusta tocar huevos de araña, grasa de trol o dedos de gigante.
Los alquimistas son diferentes. Ansían estas cosas asquerosas. Porque las necesitan para sus pociones, y porque son demasiado débiles para cazar troles ellos mismos, pagarán una prima por ingredientes y partes de animales.
Lo que es basura para un cazador es oro para un alquimista. LOS OBSERVADORES DE ESTRELLAS (Magos)
Los magos son los mejores clientes. A menudo están perdidos en sus libros y no tienen concepto del valor del oro.
Si encuentras gemas de alma, grimarios o pergaminos, llévaselos solo a un hechicero de la corte o al Colegio. Están desesperados por magia. Vaciarán sus bolsillos por una gema de alma llena sin regatear. Es casi demasiado fácil tomar sus monedas. LOS LLENABARRIGAS (Posaderos)
Skyrim es fría. Todo el mundo tiene hambre. Pero los posaderos siempre se están quedando sin suministros frescos.
Si tienes comida cruda, carne, verduras, sal, véndesela al posadero, no a los puestos del mercado. La necesitan ahora para alimentar a sus huéspedes. Un huésped hambriento se va; un huésped alimentado compra cerveza. El posadero sabe esto, y te paga por la ayuda. LA FAMILIA (Las caravanas)
Y finalmente, están los parientes de Ra'zinda. Las caravanas.
No somos bienvenidos en las ciudades. No podemos establecer tiendas. Pero tenemos... conexiones.
Si encuentras cosas que son "problemáticas" de vender, joyería, bienes de lujo o artículos que los jarls llaman "ilícitos", tráenoslos.
No preguntamos de dónde los sacaste. Solo pesamos el oro. Pagamos los mejores precios por las cosas que otros tienen demasiado miedo de tocar.
Camina por arenas cálidas, mercader. [pagebreak]
EPÍLOGO

Al viajero que sostiene este libro:

Gracias por recorrer La Ruta Dorada.

Mi objetivo era traer nueva vida a los mercados de Skyrim, haciendo que cada septim ganado se sintiera como una victoria. Espero que estos cambios hayan hecho tu viaje más rico y tus cargas un poco más ligeras.

Que tus bolsillos sean pesados y tu camino esté despejado.

— Vuszu
